asked: In DS05, is habitus worse in dogs further from the Beagle course, at a given pseudo-stage?
found: Partial rho -0.24 (95% CI -0.39 to -0.07), p 0.005, n 147; it vanishes once haematocrit is controlled (+0.08, -0.08 to 0.24). The spec stage score does not keep the Beagles' time order (rho 0.19) and the time-anchored course fails the illness-duration check: no construction passes both. Dropping one Beagle reverses the order of the dogs in 2 of 5 refits.
detectable: |rho| about 0.23 at n 147: at the edge

asked: Where do naturally infected dogs lie relative to the Beagle course?
found: Within 2 spread units of the course: 20% (13 to 30) of DS03 cohort 1 (n 85), 17% (6 to 39) of cohort 2 (n 18), 24% (18 to 32) of DS05 (n 147); 61%, 83% and 61% project onto an end of the course. The geometry recurs in a clinic and a referral hospital; the course cannot place most natural dogs.
independent_sources: SRC-A (DS03 natural = S-CB050 dogs, SV-07); SRC-F; SRC-B (course)

asked: Do published contrasts show more parasites in severe disease, inside one species and outcome class?
found: No pooled estimate: 6 units in 5 cells, largest cell 2 units. B. canis died vs survived (CB516, 8 vs 7): Hedges g of log load -0.17 (-1.19 to 0.85). Only CB141 (B. canis, ddPCR, n 222) is significant, rho 0.35 (0.23 to 0.46) with a haematological score, and in the same cohort antibody correlates more strongly and the other way, rho -0.65 (-0.73 to -0.56), n 166.
effect: g -0.17 (-1.19 to 0.85) in the only death contrast
n: 6 units; 15 dogs in the death contrast
independent_sources: 6 literature units; no B. rossi unit

asked: In 5 DS02 Beagles, do dogs at the same load differ in damage?
found: No measure shows different norms: venous lactate and habitus loss read one shared norm, haematocrit drop cannot tell. At 5% parasitaemia lactate was 1.14 mmol/L in the one low-dose dog against 1.19 to 1.44 in the high-dose dogs. Clear damage appeared only above about 10% parasitaemia. The dog that died had the most damage at its peak, but was not a residual outlier.
effect: readings: 2 of 3 one shared norm, 1 cannot tell, 0 different
detectable: No test (per-dog intervals with 1 or 2 df)

asked: Is there a published conflict on parasitaemia and severity?
found: Parasitaemia was tested in 4 units; none pair has opposite significant directions (no conflict, and no consistent cell either).

asked: Does age (under 12 months against older) change the risk of death in B. rossi?
found: 6 of 50 young and 9 of 90 adult dogs died: OR 1.23 (0.34 to 4.15); sex-stratified MH OR 1.24 (0.41 to 3.77). 0 of 3 tests q < 0.05. Died includes euthanasia for poor prognosis.
detectable: OR about 3.7 or more (or 0.28 or less)

asked: Is severe disease anaemia-dominant in young dogs and inflammatory in adults?
found: Verdict not supported. DS05 haematocrit young minus adult HL -0.02 (-0.04 to +0.01), n 55 vs 92. DS03 shows -0.06 (-0.10 to -0.025), but DS03 dogs are S-CB050 dogs and young healthy controls are lower too. No adult excess of band neutrophils or cytokine perturbation. The one lead: young DS05 dogs presented about 1 day earlier (q 0.090). 1 of 8 tests q < 0.05.
effect: HL -0.02 L/L (-0.04 to +0.01) in the independent source

asked: What study would test host genes within one breed?
found: PubMed: no canine study has genotyped dogs against babesiosis severity or outcome. Design: pit bull-type B. rossi, 142 severe + 142 mild, from about 471 cases (about 14 hospital-years), detects DEA 1 OR 3 at alpha 0.0025; OR 2 is not feasible in one breed.
detectable: OR 3 (DEA 1); OR 2 needs 330 to 500 severe dogs

asked: How many units test parasite species or genotype against severity?
found: 2 units (parasite species or genotype); parasite DNA load 1 unit.

asked: What study would test parasite genotype at a given load?
found: BrEMA1 genotype19 against the others, complicated vs uncomplicated B. rossi, adjusted for age, days sick and load: 80 complicated + 120 uncomplicated (about 229 enrolled) for an adjusted OR 2.5; death as outcome needs about 545 enrolled. A genome-wide design is hypothesis-generating only.

asked: Is the IL-8 conflict (falls with severity in B. rossi, rises in B. canis) species, or sampling time and definition?
found: No conflict inside the dog-level files: IL-8 severe minus non-severe +0.02 (-0.28 to +0.34) in S-CB050 (died 12 vs 85) and +0.15 (-0.29 to +0.56) in S-CB017 (complicated 18 vs 13). IL-8 differs only infected vs controls (-0.45 and +0.87). The B. rossi 'falls with severity' claim rests on one abstract-only article (CB037). 3 of 12 tests q < 0.05 (IL-2, GM-CSF, MCP-1 in S-CB017).

asked: Is severe disease a larger cytokine perturbation (size) or a shifted one (balance)?
found: Rule reads 'balance', weakly: balance index higher in severe dogs in both files, +0.32 (+0.02 to +0.60, p 0.070, q 0.139) in S-CB050 and +0.44 (+0.07 to +0.78) in S-CB017, carried by MCP-1 (S-CB050 +0.47, +0.22 to +0.70, q 0.052; S-CB017 +0.81). Size (perturbation count) is higher only in complicated B. canis (+0.71), whose label includes SIRS.

asked: Which markers agree in 3 or more independent units of one species and outcome class?
found: None: 0 of 423 cells reach 3 tested units; nothing pooled. Post hoc, with outcome classes merged, 4 non-circular B. rossi cells agree in 3 units (body temperature, band neutrophils, cortisol, thyroid hormones); 0 survive once Onderstepoort is counted once. Lactate is the most uniform named result (higher with death in 3 units).

asked: How are severity definitions built, and how often is a marker part of its own definition?
found: 78 definitions in 42 units. A tested marker belongs to its own definition in 38 of 504 tested rows (7 of 31 units); those rows are significant 79% of the time against 47% for other rows.

asked: Which human severity mechanisms are unmeasured against severity in dogs?
found: 37 mechanisms: 21 gaps (12 never measured in canine babesiosis); 21 of 36 with human grade 2 or 3 are gaps (58%), but 10 of 26 grade-3 mechanisms already have canine severity data. Top gaps: angiopoietin-2, VEGF/sFlt-1, NETs, histones, calprotectin. The grades are one agent's judgement, not reviewed.

asked: Do serum proteins of these mechanisms differ between complicated and uncomplicated B. rossi in DS07?
found: Not supported: none of 10 family proteins at q < 0.05 (9 tested). Haemoglobin beta +0.48 (+0.09 to +0.82), p 0.019, q 0.133, which partly restates the label (haematocrit < 0.15 and bilirubin are in the definition). Haptoglobin, alpha-2-antiplasmin, protein C, antithrombin, factor H within +/-0.12. Histone H4 untestable.
detectable: about 1.0 SD at alpha 0.05, 1.3 SD after correction

asked: Do human severe-malaria blood signatures rise in the Beagles before treatment, before deterioration, and earlier at high dose?
found: Type 1 interferon and neutrophil-granule scores rose in 5 of 5 dogs (4 of 5 beyond background each; sign p 0.0625, the smallest possible). Interferon rose before habitus fell in 5 of 5. 'Earlier at high dose' not met. Every dog rose, including the mild low-dose dogs, and the size of the rise does not separate the dog that died: a response to infection, not a severity gradient.
detectable: No sign test can reach p < 0.05 with 5 dogs

asked: After haematocrit and illness duration, is there a stable residual axis in DS05?
found: Two bootstrap-stable axes (phi 0.99, 0.96), n 140. Axis 2 (leukocytes up, regeneration down at a given haematocrit) relates to habitus, partial rho -0.26 (-0.40 to -0.10); DS05 is already seen, so exploratory. Axes are directions in a continuum, not groups of dogs.

asked: Do the DS05 axes recur in an independent file?
found: 0 of 6 axis-by-block checks replicate. Block patterns recur (phi 0.99, 1.00) but cannot be shown specific with 3 shared variables; in the only testable block (S-CB017, B. canis, n 31) phi 0.99 is no better than a uniform pattern (0.98, p 0.075). DS03 and S-CB050 are one source.
detectable: Files share only 3 to 5 of 12 variables

asked: Does the axis score separate dogs that died beyond band neutrophils?
found: S-CB050 died +0.49 (+0.21 to +0.74), q 0.003, but band neutrophils alone give +0.60 and after removing bands the score gives +0.15 (-0.17 to +0.45): it restates the published band-neutrophil finding. S-CB017 complicated +0.28 (-0.13 to +0.68). MCP-1 does not track the score.
